newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-CONFIDENT WOODS HUMBLED BY CONGRESSIONAL.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CONFIDENT WOODS HUMBLED BY CONGRESSIONAL.

text.p: A faulty putter and numerous errant drives left Tiger Woods without a chance at the U.S. Open title on Sunday and he said he had been "humbled" by the longest course in the history of the national championship.
"The suffering is over," a relieved Woods said after he shot a 72 to finish the tournament six over par. "This golf course beat me up."
The 21-year-old Masters champion showed some flashes of brilliance at his third Open, but he was unable to overcome Congressional's deep rough and slippery greens.
"I putted horrible this week. My speed was off and that made my line go off," he said.
"Any U.S. Open is going to humble you, even if you win. It's humbled me big time," said the usually supremely confident Woods.
Still, there were moments of magic that thrilled large, noisy and adoring galleries that followed Woods through all 72 holes of the grueling event.

Late in the final round, the gallery included President Bill Clinton, who watched as Woods drained a twisting 15-foot birdie putt at the 16th hole. Wood said he didn't see the president, who was in a box overlooking the green.
Overall, Woods said, "I had a good time. My patience was tested but I think I held up pretty well."
Before the tournament Woods had been the centre of attention because of his astounding record 12-stroke victory at the Masters in April.

He also brought a streak of six consecutive national titles into the Open after winning three U.S. junior crowns followed by an unprecdented three successive U.S. Amateur titles over the past six years.
But he played poorly, overshooting several greens at Congressional and missing putts the first day to shoot 74.
He came back with a 67 Friday to get back in the hunt, but three-putted three times for bogeys on the back nine Saturday, finishing the third round with a 73 to stand four over for the tournament.
Any hopes for a miracle finish were gone after three bogeys on the first five holes Sunday.
